messages:
alex.r: FYI found a batch of presigned S3 URLs for model artifacts in an internal model-sync debug snapshot that was briefly reachable from an internal dev bucket. looks like they were generated by the model-sync job and ended up in a snapshot that got indexed by an internal dev search job. potential exposure window ~3h. I'm locking down the sync job now. :rotating_light:
sec-bot: Detected suspicious GETs for presigned URL pattern from 18.205.XX.XX between 05:12-05:20 UTC. Logged as SEC-2026-112 in the incident tracker.
infra_oncall: Taking model-sync job offline now. running: `kubectl scale deployment/model-sync -n infra --replicas=0` 
maria.s: Good call. Start revoking any presigned urls we can and rotate the credentials the sync job uses. evan.k can you take the rotate?
evans.k: on it. I'll rotate the IAM keys for model-sync-sa and redeploy with new creds. ETA 30m. posting steps in #eng-oncall after done.
sre-lead: Also toggle bucket policy to block public GETs and remove any ACLs that allow ListObject or GetObject for anonymous. Quick commands: `aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket redwood-models-dev --policy file://deny-public-get.json`
alex.r: I've disabled the dev search indexing job that scraped snapshots and started a quick scan to look for other snapshots with presigned urls.
product-security: We need an internal customer impact assessment. Do we have any external customers who could have accessed these dev snapshots? If so we may need to notify.
maria.s: No evidence yet of external customer access — request: infra team to produce access logs export for the bucket and prefix `models/snapshots/` for the window 05:00-08:00 UTC. include requester IPs and user agents.
infra_oncall: Exporting logs now to s3://redwood-security-exports/SEC-2026-112/ and initiating a lifecycle tag for later retention.
sec-bot: Checklist created: [1] revoke presigned URLs (can't be individually revoked) -> rotate underlying credentials and expire URLs by changing object permissions; [2] rotate model-sync service account credentials; [3] block model publish route in Console for dev orgs until rollout; [4] enable object-level logging and MFA for model publishing; [5] notify compliance if customer data involved.
evans.k: Rotation complete. model-sync-sa access key (AKIA...) rotated, new key pushed to secrets manager, deployment restarted. logs: `deployment/model-sync restarted - 1/1 ready`
maria.s: Confirmed no other snapshots indexed with presign pattern in initial grep but continuing deeper scan.
sre-lead: Configure proxy signed access for models instead of presigned S3 URLs: plan is to issue short-lived signed URLs from our gateway that validates caller RBAC, TTL 5m. This will be a platform change but should go to canary within 2 weeks.
alex.r: Immediate mitigation checklist (short):
 - stop model-sync job (done)
 - rotate model-sync keys (done)
 - block dev search indexing (done)
 - export & review access logs (in progress)
 - temporarily disable public model publish for dev orgs (maria to confirm)
 - add a postmortem/incident doc and update runbooks (evan + sec team)

maria.s: I'll disable dev org publish routes now. also enforcing MFA on publishing token creation for the next 72h.
product-security: I'll draft a short internal advisory for customers with private deployments if we find any access. hold until logs confirm.
sec-bot: Assigned tasks: evan.k -> runbook + rotation notes; infra_oncall -> logs export & bucket policy hardening; maria.s -> publish-route lock & policy; alex.r -> scanning & postmortem.
evans.k: Creating SEC-2026-112 postmortem issue and will attach rotation commands and timelines.
maria.s: One reminder: presigned URLs are not revocable by ID. main mitigation is credential rotation + altering object permissions or bucket policy. doc link: <https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-2026-112>
alex.r: Thanks everyone. I'll post a short summary to #security-updates when we have the logs reviewed. Please add any findings to the postmortem issue. :lock_with_ink_pen:
sec-bot: Incident status: containment in progress. next update in 45m or earlier if new findings.
